analysis: What changed versus the 4am premarket brief: (1) Bank prints resolved. JPMorgan missed EPS ($5.57 vs $5.93) and revenue ($50.17B vs $51.23B) but staged a sharp premarket U-turn (from -3.8% to +1.4%) after raising 2026 NII guidance to ~$97.2B and guiding Q4 NII ~$28B, well above consensus. Goldman beat and hit its second-best revenue quarter ever (+3% premarket); Wells Fargo profit rose 6% but revenue missed (stock down). Dimon also revealed JPM reduced share buybacks in Q3. Net signal: credit is fine (provision beat, NII strong), CIB softened from Q2 — guidance, not the print, is moving bank sentiment. (2) Memory rout persisted, not reversed: US premarket memory names stayed down 2-4.5% and the KOSPI closed -5.5% with its first volatility halt since July; rotation into banks/UNH remains the tape's offset. (3) 10Y relief held: ~5.19-5.20% (-4 to -5 bps from Friday's 5.24%) as bonds reopened; Wednesday CPI (+3.6% y/y consensus) is the swing factor into the Oct 28 FOMC (19% hike odds, 76% of BofA survey expects hold). (4) META Muse Wonder got real tech-community scrutiny (642-point HN thread) — capex-payoff story now has a product attached. (5) AAPL iPhone-18-Pro order cuts are single-source (Nikkei) — fragile until confirmed; today's Welcome Home event is the company-verified catalyst. Noise: the Decart-Amazon $7B talks and the Alphabet class action are headline risk, not fundamentals.

community_signals.takeaway: Active technical discussion (642 points, 352 comments as of Oct 13) scrutinizing Meta's benchmark-parity claims and whether the $130-145B capex is producing product — aligns with Monday's +3.4% move; adds real community due-diligence signal beyond the launch headline.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed at ~7:00 AM ET after the first bank prints: Dow E-minis +0.18% (up 92 points), S&P 500 -0.13%, Nasdaq 100 -0.59%, Russell 2000 up. Tech-to-bank rotation continued, with memory-chip names the main Nasdaq drag.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance-driven bank optimism is offsetting the chip selloff at the index level — breadth into the open decides whether this reads as rotation or risk-off.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan missed Q3 (EPS $5.57 vs $5.93 expected; revenue $50.17B vs $51.23B) on a $498M securities-loss hit, but the stock swung from -3.8% to +1.4% premarket after the bank raised 2026 net interest income guidance to ~$97.2B and guided Q4 NII ~$28B (above $27.42B consensus). Dimon also disclosed reduced share buybacks in Q3.
headlines.why_it_matters: The print missed but guidance won — NII strength says rates stay a tailwind, while the buyback pullback shows Dimon stockpiling capital against his 'fiscal deficits, sticky inflation' warning.

headlines.headline: Goldman Sachs beat and reported its second-best revenue quarter ever (+3% premarket); Wells Fargo profit rose 6% but revenue fell short (stock down); UnitedHealth climbed ~2% after raising its 2026 profit forecast on tighter medical-cost spending; J&J dipped 2.7% despite a slight profit beat. Citigroup results due shortly.
headlines.why_it_matters: Bank earnings frame Q3 season — trading/IB and NII guidance are landing better than the EPS headlines, which is what actually moves sector sentiment.

headlines.headline: Memory rout continued: Micron -2.5 to -2.8%, Sandisk -3 to -4.5%, Western Digital and Seagate -3.5 to -4% premarket after China's CXMT unveiled a 4F2 memory-cell breakthrough over the weekend. South Korea's KOSPI closed -5.5% with its first volatility trading halt since July (Samsung -7.4%, SK Hynix -10%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A credible Chinese memory competitor is repricing the supply-constraint thesis that funded memory margins — the selloff is reaching a second day, so this is not a one-day headline trade.

headlines.headline: IDC data shows Nvidia's share of China's data-center AI-chip market fell to 34% in H1 2026, with Huawei at 28% and Nvidia China shipments -44% YoY; Nvidia shed ~0.5% premarket. Rotation instead favored Meta and Microsoft as 'model-agnostic' AI bets.
headlines.why_it_matters: Export controls plus Beijing's domestic push are now quantified — the China headwind for Nvidia is measured in share points, not headlines.

headlines.headline: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan's Monday warning that capital access is the biggest AI constraint, and his 'casino gambling' comparison for some AI investment flow, continued to weigh on AI-capex sentiment; Intel's CEO echoed doubts about borrowing costs and AI-investment returns.
headlines.why_it_matters: Industry leaders openly doubting AI capex economics gives the tape a fundamental cover story for derisking, beyond the CXMT headline.

headlines.headline: Apple holds its company-confirmed 'Welcome Home' smart-home event today at 9:00 AM ET in New York (online video + press hands-on). Product details (smart-home hub with A18, new Apple TV, HomePod mini 2) are single-source via Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, not officially confirmed. Separately, Nikkei Asia reports (single-source) Apple told suppliers to cut October iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by at least 15% on weak late-August-to-October demand.
headlines.why_it_matters: The event is confirmed but the iPhone demand signal is single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile: it only matters if it reappears in the Nov 2 earnings report.

headlines.headline: Microsoft is rolling out new in-house AI chips to cut dependence on Nvidia, closed Monday back above a $4T market cap, and Melius upgraded to Buy with a $665 price target; Meta and Microsoft gained premarket as investors rotated into model-agnostic AI software names.
headlines.why_it_matters: In-house silicon signals margin relief on the AI capex bill — MSFT is the megacap safe haven confirming this is rotation into quality, not broad tech selling.

headlines.headline: MIT filed a patent-infringement lawsuit against AWS over two university patents (confirmed, WSJ; typically slow-moving, minor sentiment drag). Separately, Amazon is reportedly in talks to acquire AI startup Decart for ~$7B (unconfirmed — talks could collapse), and Cantor Fitzgerald trimmed its Amazon price target $320 to $310 while keeping Overweight ahead of late-October Q3 results.
headlines.why_it_matters: Confirmed facts are mild (litigation overhang, pre-earnings target trim); the $7B deal talk is unconfirmed, so treat the expansionary read as fragile until it firms up.

headlines.headline: Meta launched 'Muse Wonder' and 'Muse Wonder Full' frontier AI models Monday, claiming benchmark parity with OpenAI/Anthropic; shares surged 3.4% Monday but slipped ~0.5% premarket. Cantor kept Overweight but cut its target $860 to $840 pre-earnings; Wells Fargo had earlier raised to $1,000. Q3 results scheduled Oct 21.
headlines.why_it_matters: A frontier model shows the $130-145B capex is producing product — the launch is now under real technical scrutiny (see HN signal), and Oct 21 earnings is the next proof point.

headlines.headline: No fresh Tesla development overnight. Carried context: Q3 deliveries of 486,532 beat ~461k consensus; Friday's NHTSA defect-petition (robotaxis speeding in active school zones) is the third federal action in ~5 weeks; Tesla is renaming 'Full Self-Driving (Supervised)' to 'Tesla Assisted Driving' on European websites after German regulator criticism.
headlines.why_it_matters: Regulatory overhang without new facts — the Oct 30 sworn-certification deadline for Cybercab answers remains the next dated catalyst.

headlines.headline: Melius (Ben Reitzes) expects a strong Google Cloud quarter at Oct 28 earnings, kept Hold on GOOGL but called AVGO/MRVL/ANET the real winners of Google's AI buildout, predicting $352B of Google 2027 AI-infrastructure spend (+75% vs 2026). Separately, a BFA law-firm press release announced a securities class action against Alphabet over Gemini 3.5 disclosures (lead-plaintiff deadline Dec 1); the allegations are unproven.
headlines.why_it_matters: A $352B 2027 capex forecast is bullish demand for Google's suppliers but keeps the capex-return debate alive; the class action is routine headline risk unless certified.

headlines.headline: 10Y Treasury yield fell ~5 bps to ~5.19% as bonds reopened after the Columbus Day holiday, helped by lower oil and the AI-stock pullback; WSJ poll consensus sees Wednesday's September CPI at +3.6% y/y (from 3.4%). Markets price a 19% chance of a hike at the Oct 28 FOMC, and 76% of BofA survey respondents expect a hold.
headlines.why_it_matters: Modest duration relief into Wednesday's CPI — the 5.365% 24-year high from last week is the line in the sand for the whole tape.

headlines.headline: IMF kept its 2026 global growth outlook unchanged and nudged its 2027 forecast higher, while warning resilience remains strained; copper prices hit record highs on China power-consumption data, offsetting some of the chip-sector gloom.
headlines.why_it_matters: The macro backdrop is neutral-to-firm — the tape's pressure is sector-specific (chips, rate sensitivity), not a global growth break.
